name: Karp
label: K
lede: Three Tumwater classmates named their band after a zine with a very rude title, put out three albums on K Records, and got picked by Beck as an opening act.

eras.title: A newsletter turns into a band
eras.text: Tumwater is a suburb just outside Olympia. Chris Smith, Jared Warren and Scott Jernigan came out of its high school with a Melvins habit and a name borrowed from Smith's newsletter.

years.src: Wikipedia: Karp (band) · The Agit Reader: What's the Rumpus? Kill All Redneck Pricks · SeanCarnage: Bill Badgley on Kill All Redneck Pricks
years.h: Chris Smith's high school newsletter becomes a band's name
years.p: That was the zine's title, and KARP is the acronym. Smith, Jared Warren and Scott Jernigan were Tumwater High classmates with the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] as the model.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the band to 1990 and says the name grew out of a newsletter Smith put out in high school. The Agit Reader gives the zine's title as Kill All Redneck Pricks, which is what KARP stands for.

Filmmaker Bill Badgley, who later made the band's documentary, was asked what he hadn't known going in. His answer: "That all three of their mothers names are Susan." He also drove about 360 miles round trip from Yakima to see them play.

eras.title: Beck's opening act
eras.text: Karp signed on with K Records, put out two albums in two years, and got pulled onto the road by one of the biggest names in the Olympia orbit.

years.cap: Chris Smith, Jared Warren and Scott Jernigan in Olympia, c. 1994
years.h: Calvin Johnson's K Records gets Karp's first album, Mustaches Wild
years.p: Riffipedia dates the record to 1994. Before it came a scatter of early 7-inches and a spot on the 1993 Julep compilation.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists the early singles I'd Rather Be Clogging and I'm Done on Punk in My Vitamins and Freighty Cat on Atlas, plus a track on Julep, a 1993 compilation from Yoyo Recordings. Riffipedia describes the band's early releases as satirical.

K is the Olympia label run by [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]], and it became Karp's home for three albums.

years.cap: Scott Jernigan drumming at the Grape Garage, Fargo, N.D., October 1994
years.src: SeanCarnage: Bill Badgley on Kill All Redneck Pricks · Riffipedia: Karp · Wikipedia: Lync · Wikipedia: Yoyo A Go Go · Discogs: Kill All Redneck Pricks DVD
years.h: Beck sees Karp at the OK Hotel and asks them on tour
years.p: Karp shared a Seattle bill with Beck and [[Lync|65e1b41c-c719-4237-9f72-c2f07ea19355]] that night, and Beck invited the band to open his Loser tour.
years.xp:
Badgley tells the OK Hotel story in his interview with SeanCarnage. He and his friends, "snobby 16 year olds" by his own description, sold their Beck tickets and left after Karp played. Riffipedia dates the U.S. tour with Beck to 1994.

The connection ran through Olympia: Lync's Sam Jayne and James Bertram played on Beck's One Foot in the Grave that year, right before Lync's own album for K. The film's DVD also carries a 39-minute extra labelled Yo Yo 94, from that summer's Yoyo A Go Go festival at the Capitol Theater.

years.p: The second K album is named for a wrestling throw. Riffipedia is the only source that dates it, to 1995.

years.h: Karp goes to Japan a year after the Beck run
years.p: Riffipedia dates the trip to 1995, one of the band's first outside the U.S.
years.xp: Riffipedia is the only source found for the date, so treat it as a lead.

eras.title: Singles on a dozen labels, then the end
eras.text: Karp scattered 7-inches across a dozen small labels, made its third K album, headlined Olympia's biggest festival, and broke up in 1998.

years.h: We Ate Sand comes out while the singles pile up
years.p: Karp kept feeding small labels: Up Records, Troubleman Unlimited, Mammoth and Atlas all got a single or a split.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists a split with [[Rye Coalition|7e6b3645-2a39-403f-b82e-31cd73d691e3]] on Troubleman Unlimited, a split with Long Hind Legs on Karate Brand, and a track on the Mammoth compilation Jabberjaw: Good to the Last Drop. Riffipedia adds splits with [[Unsane|db9cbc9e-65b6-4221-a847-75981feb1c6b]] and Chokebore.

The 1996 date on We Ate Sand is Wikipedia's; the exact 7-inch release dates elsewhere are not confirmed.

years.src: The Agit Reader: What's the Rumpus? Kill All Redneck Pricks · Riffipedia: Karp
years.h: Self Titled LP arrives with the band close to a bigger break
years.p: Of that 1997 album, the Agit Reader's Stephen Slaybaugh wrote that the band seemed "on the precipice of even greater success commercially and artistically."
years.xp: The Agit Reader's review of the documentary puts the self-titled album at 1997. Riffipedia lists it as 1996, so the year is flagged. It is the third and last of the K albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Yoyo A Go Go · Discogs: Kill All Redneck Pricks DVD
yt: Forget the Minions, Yoyo A Go Go 1997
Bastard of Disguise and J is for Genius, Yoyo A Go Go 1997
years.h: Karp tops the bill at Yoyo A Go Go
years.p: Fifty-plus bands at the Capitol Theater in Olympia, and Karp headlines alongside [[Sleater-Kinney|e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7]], [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]], [[Elliott Smith|03ad1736-b7c9-412a-b442-82536d63a5c4]] and [[Built to Spill|3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0]].
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes the 1994 festival as a punk rock slumber party and lists Karp among the 1997 headliners. Organizers leaned on DIY and community, with string quartets and puppeteers filling gaps between bands.

The documentary's DVD includes a 39-minute Yo Yo 97 extra.

years.src: The Agit Reader: What's the Rumpus? Kill All Redneck Pricks · The Stranger: Not a Fish Tale · SeanCarnage: Bill Badgley on Kill All Redneck Pricks · Riffipedia: Karp
years.h: Karp breaks up after the Prison Shake 7-inch on Up Records
years.p: Prison Shake was the last release. The Agit Reader ties the split to Chris Smith's drug use and a suicide attempt.
years.xp:
The Agit Reader says Smith struggled with heroin and later got clean. The Stranger also mentions a suicide attempt when it recounts why the band ended.

Both accounts come from coverage of Badgley's film rather than from the band. Smith was hard to find: it took Badgley about a year to track him down. By the time of the film Badgley says Smith was working as a proofreader at the Washington State Legislative Building.

eras.title: A second band that never got going
eras.text: Warren and Jernigan tried to start over as the Whip. Jernigan died before it went anywhere.

years.src: The Agit Reader: What's the Rumpus? Kill All Redneck Pricks · Wikipedia: Jared Warren
years.h: Warren and Jernigan try again as the Whip
years.p: The two reunited around 2002, per the Agit Reader, but the band never got far.
years.xp: Warren also played in Tight Bros from Way Back When after Karp, per the Agit Reader.

years.src: Wikipedia: Karp (band) · The Stranger: Not a Fish Tale · SeanCarnage: Bill Badgley on Kill All Redneck Pricks · The Agit Reader: What's the Rumpus? Kill All Redneck Pricks
years.h: Scott Jernigan dies in a boating accident on Lake Washington
years.p: Wikipedia dates the accident to June 10, 2003. Badgley left the details out of the film.
years.xp:
The Stranger calls Jernigan's death a boating accident in 2003, and Badgley told SeanCarnage the film keeps the description at that. The Agit Reader dates it to 2002, so the year is flagged.

Jernigan was the band's drummer from the start, at Tumwater High.

eras.title: The bass player's second act
eras.text: Warren took the volume up a level, then a fan took the band's whole story and put it on a screen.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jared Warren · Wikipedia: Big Business (band) · Wikipedia: Melvins
years.h: The Melvins, Karp's old model, hire Jared Warren
years.p: He joins with his Big Business partner Coady Willis, and both play on (A) Senile Animal.
years.xp:
Warren formed Big Business in 2004 with Coady Willis of the [[Murder City Devils|32705a3c-54cf-4e48-a3ab-2801157a09dc]]. Wikipedia's Jared Warren page has both joining the Melvins in January 2006; the Big Business page says late 2006.

Warren was Melvins bassist 2006 to 2015, on (A) Senile Animal (2006), Nude with Boots (2008) and The Bride Screamed Murder (2010).

years.src: The Stranger: Not a Fish Tale · Wikipedia: Karp (band) · Discogs: Kill All Redneck Pricks DVD · SeanCarnage: Bill Badgley on Kill All Redneck Pricks
years.h: A fan spends four years making Kill All Redneck Pricks
years.p: Bill Badgley of Federation X had never made a movie. He interviewed 65 people, and the film opened in Seattle at the Grand Illusion.
years.xp:
The Stranger reports the film was unfunded and took over four years, with Badgley living in a punk house and working TV jobs to pay for it. Wikipedia says a preview screened in Seattle on October 22, 2009; the DVD (Molasses Manifesto, 2011) runs 1:23:39 and adds extras from Yo Yo 94, Yo Yo 97 and Beef T.V.

It played Europe before the U.S. By mid-October, per SeanCarnage, it had shown about 45 times in 8 countries. The Seattle run at the Grand Illusion was November 25 to December 1.

years.h: Warren takes Vern Rumsey's bass spot on Unwound's reunion tour
years.p: Warren was recruited in September 2022 to fill in for the late [[Vern Rumsey|a4d62ca9-11fa-4658-90a7-71317f8f37d0]], a friend from the Olympia scene.
